S2
23
Text S1 The selection of ferrihydrite dosing and the intensity/frequency of micro-
24
aeration
25
According to our previous study, a low Fe(III) content (< 750 mg/L) promoted 
26
anaerobic digestion, while as the Fe(III) content increased to 1470 mg/L, methane 
27
production was slightly inhibited (Wang et al. 2024). Therefore, 15 mM Fe(III) in the 
28
form of ferrihydrite, containing 840 mg/L Fe(III), was selected here.
29
To prevent the potential inhibition of methanogens by excessive aeration, this 
30
study adopted a low aeration intensity (14 mL of O₂/(LReactor·day)). Furthermore, 
31
different aeration strategies have been reported; air or oxygen can be dosed either one 
32
time, intermittently (pulse-mode), or continuously (Botheju and Bakke 2011). To 
33
achieve multiple redox alternations for Fe(II) oxidation and ROS generation, the 
34
anaerobic system was aerated for 30 min every 3 h.
35
36
37

S3
38
Text S2 ROS measurement
39
The •OH formation pathways were explored by examining the intermediates (e.g., 
40
•O2- and H2O2). •OH and •O2- production was qualitatively detected by an electron 
41
paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectrometer with DMPO as a spin-trapping agent. The 
42
formation of •OH and H2O2 was determined using a fluorescence probe method with 
43
50 µM coumarin and 200 µM cerium sulfate (Liu et al. 2023, Wu et al. 2023).  
44
The parameters of electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectrometer
45
EPR instrument (Bruker, Elexsys II E500-CW-EPR) operating parameters were 
46
center field 3500 G; microwave frequency 9.8 GHz; microwave power 2.0 mW; 
47
modulation frequency 4.0 G; modulation amplitude 4.0 G; sweep width 200 G; receiver 
48
gain 3.54 × 104; time constant 41.0 ms; sweep time 15 s; 15 scans. 
49
Quantitative analysis of H2O2 and •OH
50
The H2O2 concentration was measured using the cerium sulfate titration method, 
51
where the yellow Ce4+ solution would be reduced by H2O2 to colorless Ce3+ following 
52
the stoichiometry of 2Ce4+ + H2O2 = 2Ce4+ + 2H+ + O2. The concentration of Ce4+ 
53
before and after the redox reaction can be detected by ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy. 
54
The test value at 316 nm was adopted. 1 mM of Ce4+ solution was prepared by 
55
dissolving 332 mg of Ce(SO4)2 in 0.5 M of H2SO4 solution(1L). The H2O2 
56
concentration is calculated by the equation of
57
C(H2O2)= (C0(Ce4+)×V(Ce4+) - C(Ce4+)×(V(Ce4+)+V(H2O2)))/(2×V(H2O2))
58
The oxidation product of coumarin by •OH, i.e., 7-hydroxylcoumarin (7h-COU), 
59
was measured at an excitation of 350 nm and an emission of 460 nm using a microplate 
60
reader. Then, the concentration of •OH was calculated according to 7h-COU/14.5%.
61
62

S4
63
Text S3 Characterization and analysis
64
1. Morphology characterization
65
X-ray diffraction (XRD) was applied for the identification of the crystalline iron 
66
phases in digesters. The XRD diffractometer (SmartLab 9kw, Japan) equipped a Cu-
67
Ka radiation (45 kV, 200 mA) at a scan rate was 8°/min, between 5° and 80° (Wang et 
68
al. 2022).
69
2. Electrochemical measurement
70
After washing three times with 0.01 M phosphate buffer solution (PBS), 20 μL of 
71
the sediment suspensions were coated on a glassy carbon electrode (Φ3 mm, working 
72
area: 0.07 mm2) and dried in an infrared oven. Electrochemical tests were performed 
73
with an electrochemical workstation (Chenhua, CHI 660). The coated glassy carbon 
74
electrode, Ag/AgCl electrode, and Pt electrode were selected as the working electrode, 
75
reference electrode, and counter electrode, respectively. The capacitance and resistance 
76
of the sediment were assessed with cyclic voltammetry (CV) and electrochemical 
77
impedance spectroscopy (EIS), respectively.   
78
Cyclic voltammetry was performed in the range of -0.8 to 0.8 V (vs Ag/AgCl) at 
79
scan rates of 50 mV/s, with 30 mL of 0.01 M PBS as the electrolyte. Electrochemical 
80
impedance spectroscopy was conducted over a frequency range of 1000 kHz to 0.01 Hz, 
81
with a sinusoidal perturbation of 10 mV amplitude to analyze the internal impedances 
82
of the sediments. Before the electrochemical tests, the electrolyte in the same 
83
concentration was aerated for 40 min with N2 to maintain an anaerobic condition.
84
3. Analytical methods
85
TSS, VSS, and COD were determined by the Standard Methods for the 
86
Examination of Water and Wastewater (Wang et al. 2018). The volume and content of 
87
biogas were measured using a 100 mL glass syringe and a gas chromatograph (Tianmei,

S5
88
GC-7900, China) with a thermal conductivity detector (TCD), respectively (Zhao et al. 
89
2015).
90
Determination of total Fe(II)
91
A 0.5 mL homogeneous sample was taken from the reactor to detect Fe(II) 
92
concentration. 1 mL HCl (6 M) was added to the sample immediately after collection 
93
to inhibit the oxidation of Fe2+ to Fe3+. Total Fe(II) content was analyzed by a modified 
94
1,10-o-phenanthroline analytical method. Briefly, after two hours of acid leaching, 0.5 
95
mL supernatant after centrifugation was mixed with 1 mL hydroxylamine 
96
hydrochloride solution (10% w/v) and boiled for 20 min to quantify total Fe. Then the 
97
sample was mixed with 5 mL iron buffer solution (40% w/v ammonium acetate in 50% 
98
v/v glacial acetic acid) and 2 mL 1,10-o-phenanthroline solution (0.5% w/w). The 1,10-
99
o-phenanthroline was given 15 min to react with Fe(II) before absorbance at 510 nm 
100
was measured.
101
Determination of phenol
102
The concentration of phenol was quantified using HPLC equipped with UV–vis 
103
detector (Waters, 2489) and a C18 column (5 μm, 4.6 mm × 250 mm), the mobile phase 
104
(flow rate of 1 mL/min) was the mixture consisting of methanol and H2O (70:30, V/V), 
105
and determined by UV mode at 282 nm, respectively. 
106

S6
107
Text S4 Metagenomic sequencing and analysis.
108
Total DNA from aggregates in each UASB digester was extracted by E.Z.N.A™ 
109
Mag-Bind Soil DNA Kit (OMEGA, M5635-02, USA). The concentrations of the 
110
extracted DNA were determined by a spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher, Q33238, 
111
USA). Fragmentation buffer solutions were added into the qualified DNA samples that 
112
were randomly interrupted into the short DNA fragments by ultrasound. The short DNA 
113
fragments were used for library construction. Metagenomic sequencing was conducted 
114
by Sangon Biotech (Shanghai) Co. Ltd, China using an Illumina HiSeq 2500 platform. 
115
To ensure the reliability of data, the raw reads were pre-processed using a Trimmomatic 
116
software to obtain high-quality clean reads (Bolger et al. 2014). Quality control was 
117
performed with FastQC (Schmieder and Edwards 2011). Clean reads were assembled 
118
using a MEGAHIT software to obtain contigs (Li et al. 2015). Open reading frames 
119
(ORFs) in the contigs were predicted using a Prodigal software. Gene clustering and 
120
redundancy removal were performed to obtain a non-redundant gene catalogue 
121
(Unigenes) using a Mmseqs software (Steinegger and Soeding 2017). Clean reads after 
122
quality control were blasted with the gene catalogue to calculate the different Unigene 
123
levels using a bbmap software (Holmes et al. 2017). Protein sequences were aligned to 
124
KEGG database to obtain the functional information (Huerta-Cepas et al. 2017).

S7
125
Text S5 Economic Analysis of the Process of Intermittent Micro-aeration Coupled with 
126
Ferrihydrite Addition
127
The economic feasibility was evaluated on a 1 m³ reactor with the same O2 supply 
128
and ferrihydrite addition as the experiment in this study. In practical engineering 
129
applications, O2 could be replaced by ambient air with equivalent O2 content to save 
130
cost. The cost primarily consists of aeration expenses and ferrihydrite procurement 
131
costs, while the revenue can be derived from the increased methane production.
132
Specifically, the aeration energy consumption was 0.1 CNY/day (50 W × 4 h/day 
133
× 0.5 CNY/kW·h). The cost of a single ferrihydrite addition (15 mM Fe(III), calculated 
134
as Fe₅HO₈·4H₂O) was 43.2 CNY (15 mM × 1000 L × 0.096 kg × 30 CNY/kg). The 
135
daily revenue generated from methane yield increase amounts to 1.22 CNY/day (0.67 
136
m³/day × 1.82 CNY/m³). Therefore, the system reached break-even after approximately 
137
39 days (43.2 CNY /(1.22 CNY/day - 0.1 CNY/day)).
138
